# Minimal joint-output connector charge

## Summary

Refines the `connector-alphabet-change` card to the smallest nonzero instance
of one output-side operation:

```text
J_ik: (y_i, y_k) += (A_i z, A_k z)
```

With one source, one arbitrarily dirty connector and two arbitrarily dirty
targets, `J_ik, B, J_ik, B` computes both requested outputs and restores the
connector for arbitrary fixed `F_2`-linear maps. A dimension-independent
additivity proof accompanies an exhaustive check of all 1,048,576 combinations
of 2x2 maps and data states, plus three failure controls.

The complete bill charges both output-map evaluations and both targets on
every `J_ik`. If `D` is one root dispatch and `phi` is the extra joint-routing
and fusion overhead, the original schedule costs
`2c_B+2c_i+2c_k+6D`, while the extended schedule costs
`2c_B+2c_i+2c_k+4D+2phi`. The operation improves the completed bill exactly
when `phi<D`; leaf map work is unchanged. The package does not claim a physical
one-record implementation or supplier benefit.

## Source and scope

Base `20ecf2891d80b5acf18d980b2164fb44ea7faa90`, priority revision 6.
The package is `research/joint-output-connector-minimal-charge-247794/`; exact
source blobs and SHA256 hashes are recorded in `SOURCES.json`.

The source-side pair operation is already covered by PR #2056, including dirty
replay and charged accesses. PR #3604's specialized P112 co-delivery is
adjacent but distinct: it shares tetrad products with a fused port and source
correction, and this package neither re-audits nor claims that factorization.
The live PR #3779 addresses a six-window restoration bill. No selected result,
supplier, or frontier changes here; there is no new κ.

Credit the fixed-alphabet and pair-source connector predecessors. Prepared by
OpenAI Codex with substantial assistance. No independent human or formal
proof-kernel review is claimed.

The registered replay left the worktree clean. This supersedes any earlier pending note above for the registered package replay; separate full selected cold-replay limits remain as stated.
